title: The grey block of Trinity on his left
html_source: Trinity College, the only college of Dublin University, stands opposite the Bank of Ireland on College Green. Trinity, an Elizabethan foundation, was Protestant and Anglo-Irish in its orientation. Catholics, who had long been denied entrance to it, were, from the 1870s, prohibited from entering it by the dictate of the Irish Catholic hierarchy. At the turn of the century, it was especially regarded as ‘foreign’ because it was hostile to the various revival movements, political and cultural, that had emerged.
